architecture_principles: physical discovery comes before candidate ranking
the Agent uses measured rheological regularities as scientific tools rather than optimizing benchmark recovery
state-aware rheology, external chemistry evidence and process uncertainty serve distinct scientific roles
candidate selection should maximize usefulness and interpretability for the observed material failure mode
deterministic calculations are separated from language-model judgment
the Skeptic and Robustness Adjudicator are decision-quality controls, not components that need ablation to justify their existence
the final recommendation is frozen before physical adjudication
only concise auditable outputs are stored; hidden chain-of-thought is not scientific evidence
held-out result data are structurally removed before outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction payloads are assembled
external analogue percentages define supported regions, not exact local optima
performance mitigation and causal isolation are distinct experiment intents; single-factor attribution is not the universal default
among similarly supported candidates, the minimum sufficient intervention is preferred
architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V3.4.0 is an outcome-blind reconstruction of the preexperimental decision state using only evidence available before the validation result. It may support recovery of the scientific problem, intervention family, and formulation neighborhood, but it must not be described as a recovered contemporaneous machine record or as proof that the exact historical recipe was independently predicted.

evaluation_priority: physical wet-lab adjudication of the selected point
traceable use of measured local regularities

architecture.name: PUR_NEW_PREEXPERIMENTAL_RECONSTRUCTION_AGENT_V3
non_goals: proving that every internal Agent module is individually necessary through ablation
making architecture benchmarking the main scientific contribution
optimizing held-out-region recovery as the main objective
claiming that literature-prior proximity predicts the wet-lab outcome
replacing the material-science result with an LLM-systems paper
primary_agent_outputs: material regularities used in the decision
design implication derived from each regularity
measurement plan tied to the discovered failure mode
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that reconstructs the preexperimental decision state: it extracts material-response regularities from measured PUR rheology, selects an intervention strategy, and freezes one useful formulation-process experiment point without access to the later validation formulation or outcome.
required_scientific_sequence: state the positive material regularities and their boundaries
translate those regularities into a design objective
use external evidence to identify chemically plausible intervention directions
adjudicate robustness to reasonable alternative evidence interpretations
freeze one useful experiment point and a falsifiable measurement criterion
architecture.secondary_replay_role: Deprecated for the current study narrative. The active Stage-1 evaluation is a single outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction, not an Arm A/Arm B replay comparison.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode, upstream rheological regularities, evidence needs and measurement objective before candidate ranking
execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, formulation inspection and process-state audits
rank experiment points according to scientific usefulness for the discovered material problem
try to falsify the provisional recommendation and test scientific interpretability, leakage and claim boundaries
adjudicate whether the proposed point remains useful under alternative evidence priorities, process-state uncertainty and the skeptic's strongest objections
resolve proposer, skeptic and robustness records and make the final pre-result decision
programmatically validate and freeze the recommendation with timestamp, hashes, model, candidate state, uncertainty and falsifiable acceptance criterion

deterministic_decision_diagnostics.intervention_sufficiency_rule: Decision order is: failure mode -> experiment intent -> required intervention-axis coverage -> evidence-supported candidates -> minimum sufficient intervention. For performance_mitigation, candidates covering EVERY independently supported axis (acrylic_like, minor_tackifier_like) are compared first. Minimum sufficient intervention is a tie-break WITHIN that group only. A candidate that zeroes an independently supported axis is a partial-coverage / mechanistic control, not the default performance rank-1; it must not become rank-1 merely because zeroing that axis lowers modifier burden.
deterministic_decision_diagnostics.note: These are transparent decision diagnostics, not fitted property predictions. Exact literature-anchor distance is retained only for audit and is not a primary ranking objective. Performance-mitigation and causal-isolation scenarios are separated so that single-factor attribution is not the default for every experiment.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

acceptance_criterion.claim: S1C40 is ready for an interpretable full-coverage performance-mitigation experiment only after the uncertainty probe establishes comparable stoichiometry, controlled process history, adequate repeatability, and valid state calibration.
acceptance_criterion.criterion: Before performance adjudication, verify AC1920 and TK100 reactive-group content, recalculate the actual NCO:OH ratio and predeclare its allowable deviation; freeze conditioning, mixing, reaction, sample-age, batch, operator, and thermal-history metadata; predeclare independent-preparation and repeat-run counts, SI aggregation, uncertainty estimation, and quantitative initial-viscosity and 80-130 C temperature-response bounds; and demonstrate that raw and state-calibrated comparisons meet the predeclared state-transfer discrepancy limit.
acceptance_criterion.failure_condition: Do not freeze S1C40 as a performance candidate if reactive stoichiometry cannot be verified, process history cannot be matched, repeatability is comparable to the predeclared mitigation threshold, state calibration fails its validity check, or quantitative viscosity and temperature-response bounds cannot be established.

judge_normalized.selection_rationale: The measured local evidence establishes formulation-dependent 120 C hold drift and substantial realization/process-state variation; paper-derived rheological rules require separate measurement of static viscosity, temperature response, and matched thermal-hold drift, with state-aware calibration used only where transfer is validated. Curated PUR literature/database priors support an acrylic-like modifier family in a broad region and a minor tackifier-like axis near 5 wt% or below about 10 wt%, but they do not predict the held-out result or establish an optimum or molecular mechanism. Under the declared performance_mitigation intent, both independently supported axes must remain covered; therefore S1C40 remains the conditional primary performance candidate, while S1C41 and S1C45 are robustness alternatives and S1C10 is only a causal control. However, the Skeptic's objections are decisive before freezing a performance point: candidate stoichiometry is unknown, process-history uncertainty is high, replicate and SI decision rules are underspecified, usable-viscosity bounds are absent, and state-model transfer is unverified. The Robustness Adjudicator correctly preserves S1C40's conditional ranking and rejects a rank reversal to a partial-coverage point, but recommends an uncertainty probe. The minimum-burden principle is applied only within sufficient full-coverage candidates; it is not used to remove either supported axis. No exact analogue distance is used as a primary objective. The next action is therefore to resolve stoichiometry, process-state, repeatability, state-transfer, and acceptance-rule uncertainties before executing the full mitigation experiment.

candidate_evaluation_dimensions: Thermal-hold stability at 120 C over 15-60 and 15-90 min using SI=(eta_t1-eta_t0)/eta_t0
Viscosity level at a temperature within the measured 80-130 C support
Temperature-response slope or state-aware temperature-sensitivity coordinate over measured support
State-calibrated versus uncalibrated prediction consistency, as indicated by the upstream summary
Acrylic modifier fraction and modifier functionality as separate, bounded axes
Minor tackifier fraction as a separate bounded axis
Compatibility with the E2 reactive-core anchor and stoichiometric feasibility
Evidence coverage and extrapolation distance from directly measured or commensurate analogue regions
Information value for distinguishing mitigation from an apparent state or process-history effect
counterfactual_checks: Would the apparent improvement persist after one-point state calibration, or is it explainable by a different realization/process state?
Would the candidate still be preferred if viscosity level were held comparable to E2 and only thermal-hold drift were considered?
Would the candidate still be preferred if the nominal viscosity were replaced by replicate distributions rather than a single value?
Does the candidate reduce the 120 C hold drift without merely shifting the response to an unsupported temperature or time region?
Is the observed benefit attributable to the supported modifier intervention direction, or could it result from altered stoichiometry, processing history, or initial state?
Would a single-axis candidate provide more causal information, and if so, is that information worth sacrificing the stated performance-mitigation objective?
Does the candidate remain defensible when external 15-20 wt% acrylic and below-about-10 wt% tackifier guidance are treated as bounded directional priors rather than an optimum?
If the candidate fails to reduce hold drift, would the result distinguish chemistry intervention failure from state calibration or repeatability uncertainty?
planner.decision_goal: Select one pre-result experiment point that mitigates thermal-hold viscosity drift while maintaining a usable viscosity level and measured temperature response, without treating external analogue percentages as an exact optimum.
design_implications: Use performance_mitigation rather than default single-factor causal isolation because the thermal-hold failure is already established and the immediate objective is to reduce it.

A multi-component intervention is admissible if each active modifier axis is independently supported, the reactive-core anchor remains physically and stoichiometrically feasible, and the combined composition remains within the bounded candidate lattice.
Evaluate candidates on hold-stability drift, viscosity level at an in-support anchor temperature, temperature-response behavior, repeatability, process-history sensitivity, and extrapolation risk.
Do not optimize only nominal viscosity; require a thermal-hold trajectory over the same 120 C and 15-90 min window used for the original comparison.
Preserve the original E2 reactive-core anchor unless a candidate-specific stoichiometric or process constraint justifies a bounded change.

Treat external numeric values as directly commensurate only when units, temperature, response definition, and formulation context match; treat the supplied acrylic and tackifier literature values primarily as directional/noncommensurate formulation-family evidence.
Use conservative lattice bounds and measured temperature/time support as experimental-design controls against extrapolation, not as evidence of an optimum.
Keep process-history, realization-state, and stoichiometric uncertainty explicit in candidate adjudication.
material_regularities_to_use: All measured temperature sweeps decrease monotonically in viscosity from 80 to 130 C, so temperature response is distinct from thermal-hold drift.
The temperature-sweep data are supported over 80-130 C; extrapolation outside this range should not guide the next point.
E1 and E5 have strongly different thermal-hold drift at 120 C over the measured 15-90 min window.
E2 shows substantial nominal repeat/run spread, so a single viscosity value should not be treated as a definitive formulation property.
The state-shift and state-aware model findings must determine whether process-state calibration is needed before comparing candidate viscosities.
External acrylic anchors near 15-20 wt% are directional or analogue evidence, not exact local optima.
External evidence supports a minor tackifier axis below about 10 wt% as a conservative design region, but does not establish local hold stability.
Comparative external evidence suggests modifier identity and reactive-group density may affect hot-hold behavior, but rheology alone cannot establish the molecular mechanism.
planner.physical_failure_mode: Thermal-hold instability is the primary established failure mode: the original E5 formulation shows a large viscosity increase at 120 C (SI 0.515 from 15 to 60 min and 0.931 from 15 to 90 min), compared with E1 (SI 0.095 and 0.168). Nominal viscosity is also not a fully reliable material property because E2 temperature-sweep repeatability is poor, with CV approximately 0.46-0.58 and maximum/minimum ratios approximately 2.8-3.6. The next experiment must therefore address hold drift while separating viscosity level, thermal response, and realization/process-state effects.
required_measurements_for_adjudication: Temperature sweep over the supported 80-130 C range with replicate runs and explicit run/process-history recording
Thermal-hold trajectory at 120 C using the original 15, 30, 60, and 90 min schedule or an explicitly justified equivalent
Initial viscosity and viscosity change at each hold time, preserving source units and calculating SI
At least one replicate or repeat preparation sufficient to characterize realization/process-state spread
State or conditioning metadata needed for the one-point calibration identified by the state-aware rheology summary
Composition and stoichiometric verification for all reactive and modifier components
A comparison against the original E1/E5 hold reference using the same response definition and temperature
Adjudication of whether the candidate remains within measured temperature/time support and the predeclared candidate-space bounds
uncertainty_triggers: The state-aware summary shows a material state shift large enough that candidate ranking depends on calibration rather than formulation alone.
Candidate viscosity is outside the 80-130 C measured support or hold duration exceeds the original 15-90 min window.
Repeatability remains comparable to or larger than the expected candidate improvement.
A candidate changes acrylic functionality, tackifier identity, or reactive-core stoichiometry beyond the evidence-supported bounded region.
The candidate's initial viscosity is improved but its hold trajectory is missing, incomplete, or measured under a different thermal history.
External evidence is being used as an exact local percentage despite noncommensurate chemistry, units, temperature, or stability endpoint.
Process history, conditioning, batch identity, or stoichiometric values are unknown or inconsistent across comparisons.
The candidate requires a mechanism claim that cannot be supported by the rheology measurements.

provisional_acceptance_criterion.claim: The candidate provides a meaningful thermal-hold mitigation relative to the established E5 failure without relying on an apparent state or process-history shift.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.criterion: Under matched 120 C processing and state-calibrated comparison, require SI15-60 <= 0.26 and SI15-90 <= 0.47, corresponding to at least a provisional 50% reduction from the E5 drift values of 0.515 and 0.931, with the improvement supported by replicate or repeat-realization data and no loss of interpretable temperature response within 80-130 C.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.failure_condition: Reject the mitigation claim if either SI criterion is exceeded, if the apparent improvement disappears after state calibration, if repeatability is comparable to the expected improvement, or if the hold trajectory is incomplete or measured outside the matched temperature/time window.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.measurement_window: 120 C at 15, 30, 60, and 90 min, with replicate or repeat realization and the same SI definition used for E1/E5.

provisional_measurement_plan.primary_response: Matched thermal-hold viscosity trajectory at 120 C at 15, 30, 60, and 90 min, calculating SI15-60 and SI15-90 from the same response definition used for E1 and E5; also measure an 80-130 C temperature sweep with replicates and record viscosity level separately from drift.
provisional_measurement_plan.state_anchor_plan: Use a state-specific in-range viscosity anchor at 120 C on each realization before or at the start of the hold, with complete conditioning, mixing history, reaction history, sample age, and operator metadata. Compare candidates using state-calibrated response where appropriate, while retaining the raw viscosity and hold trajectory.
provisional_measurement_plan.time_window: 15-90 min, with required measurements at 15, 30, 60, and 90 min; include replicate preparation or repeat realization and a supported 80-130 C temperature sweep.

regularities_used: Measured local evidence: E5 exhibits much larger 120 C viscosity drift than E1, with SI15-60 of 0.515 and SI15-90 of 0.931 versus 0.095 and 0.168 for E1.
Measured local evidence: E2 has substantial repeatability spread, including approximately 0.46-0.58 coefficient of variation and maximum/minimum ratios up to approximately 3.6 near 120 C.

Derived local model rule: realization/process state primarily shifts viscosity scale while a transferable thermal-response shape remains supported; state-aware shared-shape R2 is 0.998 versus formulation-only held-temperature error factor 1.44.
Derived local measurement rule: thermal-hold stability, static viscosity, and temperature response must be measured separately.
Measured local support rule: temperature sweeps are supported only over 80-130 C, and the matched hold test should use 120 C over the original 15-90 min window.

External analogue evidence: acrylic-like modifiers are supported as a coarse family in a broad 15-25 wt% region, with repeated approximately 19-20 wt% examples and a 25 wt% lower-OH acrylic stability comparison.
External analogue evidence: minor tackifier-like modifiers are repeatedly represented near approximately 5 wt%, with conservative guidance below about 10 wt%.
Conservative design principle: for performance mitigation, both independently supported modifier axes should be covered before applying minimum sufficient intervention.
Unresolved uncertainty: external compositions and reported stability endpoints are not exact local optima and do not establish a molecular mechanism for the local formulation.
proposer.scientific_target: Mitigate the established 120 C thermal-hold viscosity drift while retaining a usable viscosity level and measured temperature response, using the E2 reactive-core anchor and explicitly controlling realization/process-state uncertainty.
unresolved_questions: Does S1C40 reduce thermal-hold drift through formulation intervention or only through a different realization/process state?
Is the 2.5 wt% TK100 level sufficient, or is the 5 wt% level in S1C41 needed for a robust response?
Does increasing acrylic-like loading from 15 wt% to 17.5 wt% improve stability without compromising usable viscosity?
What is the verified reactive-group content and effective stoichiometric contribution of AC1920 and TK100?
Can the state-aware shared thermal-response model be transferred beyond the measured reactive-core-only local chemistry family?
Will candidate temperature-sweep repeatability remain within a range that permits adjudication of the expected hold-drift improvement?
Do the candidates preserve processability and a usable viscosity level at an in-support temperature, independently of the hold-stability result?

The evidence supports a modifier family and bounded region rather than an exact optimum; further composition refinement should follow measured hold trajectories, not exact distance to literature percentages.

alternative_comparison.scientific_tradeoff: Tests a stronger acrylic intervention with full coverage, but increases burden and relies more heavily on noncommensurate analogue-region interpretation.

alternative_comparison.scientific_tradeoff: Cleaner attribution and lower burden, but it omits the independently supported acrylic axis and is not adequate as the default performance-mitigation experiment.

required_conditions: Verify AC1920 and TK100 functionality and reactive-group content, recalculate the actual NCO:OH ratio, and define an allowable stoichiometric deviation before execution.
Freeze and record conditioning, mixing, reaction, sample-age, batch, operator, and thermal-history metadata for every realization.
Prespecify independent-preparation and repeat-run counts, SI aggregation and uncertainty methods, and a repeatability threshold relative to the proposed 50% reduction target.
Add quantitative acceptance bounds for initial viscosity and temperature-response behavior within 80-130 C.
Define an explicit state-transfer validity check comparing raw and state-calibrated results.
Retain S1C41 as the predefined full-coverage robustness follow-up if S1C40 is inconclusive or shows loading-sensitive behavior.
State that the SI15-60 and SI15-90 thresholds are conservative criteria reconstructed from local E5 measurements, not literature thresholds or predicted outcomes.
Document the outcome-blind provenance of the candidate grid and confirm that no validation identity or result influenced ranking.

robustness_checks.detail: S1C40 directly tests the established 120 C thermal-hold viscosity-drift failure using the matched 15-90 min window rather than relying on nominal viscosity alone.

The declared intent is performance_mitigation, so simultaneous coverage of both independently supported acrylic_like and minor_tackifier_like axes is scientifically appropriate; a single-axis control would be cleaner only for causal_isolation.

S1C40 covers both supported intervention axes and has the lowest total modifier burden among the leading full-coverage candidates. Its rank is not justified by burden alone because it also has complete axis coverage.

S1C40 remains inside the supported acrylic region and bounded tackifier region when literature evidence is treated as a region or directional prior; its selection does not require exact distance optimization.

S1C41 and S1C45 provide plausible higher-loading robustness tests. Scenario results show S1C40 is rank 1 in only 0.75 of scenarios, while S1C41 and S1C45 remain frequent top-three alternatives, so the rank separation is conditional.

All process-history fields are missing, E2 shows large realization spread, and transfer of the state-aware model beyond the measured reactive-core family is unverified. Apparent improvement could therefore reflect state or conditioning differences.
AC1920 and TK100 reactive-group content is unspecified, so the actual candidate NCO:OH ratio is not established despite preserving the nominal E2 core proportions.

The proposed 120 C hold trajectory, supported 80-130 C sweep, state anchor, and matched SI comparison are appropriate, but independent-preparation counts, SI uncertainty rules, quantitative viscosity bounds, and state-transfer validity criteria remain underspecified.

The intervention direction is supported by multiple independent analogue sources, but expected efficacy, functionality equivalence, stoichiometry, and the claim that 2.5 wt% tackifier is sufficient remain unverified.

The Skeptic identified serious execution and interpretability problems, but not a reason to prefer a partial-coverage candidate or abandon full-coverage mitigation. These issues warrant an uncertainty probe and conditions, not a rank reversal.

counterfactual_failures: The proposal does not establish in advance how S1C40 will be judged if state-calibrated hold drift improves but raw viscosity or temperature response shifts substantially.
It does not specify a quantitative test for whether the candidate remains preferred when initial viscosity is held comparable to E2 and only hold drift is considered.
A failure of S1C40 would not cleanly distinguish chemistry-intervention failure from state calibration error, repeatability noise, or stoichiometric misassignment.

The proposal does not provide a predeclared rule for interpreting a result in which S1C41 outperforms S1C40, which would challenge the minimum-burden tie-break but not necessarily the full intervention strategy.

critical_findings.evidence: The local E2 NCO:OH=1.80 applies only to the original reactive core, while AC1920 and possibly TK100 may contribute reactive groups. S1C40 has no verified functionality, reactive-group content, or recalculated NCO:OH value; all candidate scorecards also report six missing process fields.
critical_findings.issue: Reactive stoichiometry is not yet physically established for the proposed composition.

critical_findings.evidence: S1C40 is explicitly marked with high process-history uncertainty and six missing process fields. E2 shows CV values of approximately 0.46-0.58 and maximum/minimum ratios up to approximately 3.57 at 120 C, while the proposed improvement is evaluated against a fixed threshold without a prespecified variance or replicate decision rule.
critical_findings.issue: Process-history and realization uncertainty is large enough to confound the proposed mitigation claim.

critical_findings.evidence: The diagnostics correctly define minimum sufficient intervention only as a ranking tie-break within the full-coverage group. No evidence yet establishes that 15 wt% acrylic plus 2.5 wt% tackifier is sufficient to reduce hold drift, so the wording should be changed to 'lowest-burden full-coverage candidate within the predeclared supported band.'
critical_findings.issue: The phrase 'minimum sufficient full-coverage performance test' overstates what is known.

critical_findings.evidence: SI15-60 <= 0.26 and SI15-90 <= 0.47 are exactly 50% of the E5 values. They are labeled provisional, but the decision rule should explicitly state that the 50% reduction target is a predeclared conservative design principle, not a measured literature threshold or local efficacy estimate.
critical_findings.issue: The proposed acceptance criterion contains a reconstructed conservative rule that could be mistaken for a directly measured or literature-derived fact.

critical_findings.evidence: The stated goal includes maintaining a usable viscosity level, but the provisional criterion only specifies SI thresholds and a vague requirement for 'no loss of interpretable temperature response.' No in-support viscosity range, allowable state-calibrated deviation, or temperature-response slope criterion is supplied.
critical_findings.issue: Usable viscosity and interpretable temperature response lack quantitative acceptance criteria.

critical_findings.evidence: S1C40 simultaneously activates acrylic_like and minor_tackifier_like axes. This is acceptable for the stated performance-mitigation intent, but a favorable result cannot support attribution to either axis, and a failure cannot distinguish insufficient acrylic, insufficient tackifier, interaction, stoichiometry, or process-state effects.
critical_findings.issue: The combined intervention cannot identify the contribution of either modifier axis.

critical_findings.evidence: The upstream model has state-aware R2 of 0.9977 only within the measured local reactive-core chemistry family, while S1C40 introduces both AC1920 and TK100. The proposal acknowledges this boundary but still relies on state-calibrated comparison without defining a transfer-failure diagnostic.
critical_findings.issue: Transfer of the state-aware shared-shape model to S1C40 is not established.

critical_findings.evidence: S1C40 and S1C41 both have full coverage and strong analogue-region support. S1C40 is preferred mainly because its total modifier burden is lower; scenario stability shows S1C40 rank-1 in 0.75 of scenarios while S1C41 remains in the top three in 0.75, indicating a burden-based and scenario-sensitive distinction rather than demonstrated performance superiority.
critical_findings.issue: The rank separation between S1C40 and S1C41 is not strongly supported by evidence.

interpretability_failures: The experiment is interpretable as a test of the combined mitigation strategy, but not as a causal test of acrylic versus tackifier effects.
Unknown AC1920 and TK100 reactive-group content can change effective stoichiometry and create an alternative explanation for any hold response.
No quantitative criterion defines acceptable initial viscosity or temperature-response behavior within 80-130 C.
The replicate requirement is underspecified: 'at least one replicate or repeat realization' does not define the number of independent preparations, aggregation method, or repeatability threshold.
A favorable result could still reflect a different conditioning, batch, operator, or reaction state unless matched state metadata and anchor agreement are used as explicit validity checks.

leakage_check.detail: No explicit validation formulation identity or wet-lab outcome is exposed, and the runtime tools state that validation information was not used. However, the payload also states that the current exact V2 grid and fine-refinement software were formalized after the validation experiment and that no repository freeze artifact is available. The outcome-blind provenance of the operational grid therefore cannot be independently verified from the supplied record.

regularity_alignment.detail: The proposal correctly prioritizes the established 120 C hold-drift failure, uses full intervention-axis coverage for a performance-mitigation intent, separates static viscosity from hold stability, preserves the E2 core proportions, and treats literature percentages as analogue or bounded directional evidence. Qualification is required because the rank-1 rationale still describes S1C40 as a 'minimum sufficient' intervention before intervention sufficiency has been demonstrated, and because its apparent advantage over S1C41 is principally a burden tie-break rather than evidence of superior mitigation.

required_corrections: Replace 'minimum sufficient' with 'lowest-burden full-coverage candidate within the predeclared supported band' until sufficiency is experimentally established.
Verify AC1920 and TK100 reactive-group content and recalculate the actual candidate NCO:OH ratio before execution; define the allowable stoichiometric deviation.
Complete and freeze conditioning, mixing, reaction, sample-age, batch, operator, and thermal-history metadata for every realization.
Prespecify independent-preparation and repeat-run counts, the method for estimating SI uncertainty, and the repeatability threshold relative to the proposed 50% improvement.
Add quantitative acceptance bounds for initial viscosity and temperature-response behavior within the supported 80-130 C range.
Define an explicit state-transfer validity check, including the acceptable discrepancy between raw and state-calibrated comparisons.
State explicitly that the 50% E5 reduction thresholds are conservative design criteria reconstructed from local E5 measurements, not literature facts or predicted outcomes.
Retain S1C41 as a clearly labeled robustness follow-up rather than treating S1C40's lower modifier burden as evidence of better expected performance.
Resolve or document the provenance of the post-validation V2 grid and confirm that no held-out formulation identity or outcome-derived rule influenced candidate ranking.

scientific_boundary_check.detail: The proposal generally respects the boundaries between local measured evidence, external analogue evidence, rheological descriptors, and mechanism claims. Boundary uncertainty remains because S1C40 lies outside the chemistry family used to establish the shared-shape state model, and because modifier functionality, stoichiometry, process history, and candidate-specific hold behavior are not yet measured.

minor_tackifier_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 5% represents the repeatedly documented minor-resin region and 10% is a conservative coarse upper level.

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.

tool_trace.name: query_external_priors
tool_trace.reason: Use curated external evidence only to refine chemically plausible intervention directions and bounded regions after local diagnosis; preserve the distinction between analogue numeric anchors, directional comparative evidence, and conservative extrapolation controls.
